post.description: Mirrors the seller catalog. Products absent from the submitted array are deleted, so `products` is required: omitting it is rejected rather than treated as an empty catalog. An explicitly empty array is honoured and clears the catalog.

products.description: The complete catalog as the client holds it. Anything omitted here is deleted server-side. Omitting the field entirely is rejected with 400 products_required — it is never read as an empty catalog.

valid.summary: Full mirror of a one-product catalog

empty_catalog.summary: Seller has deleted every product; the empty array is explicit

patch.summary: Advance an order through its pipeline
patch.description:
Moves one order to the next state, or cancels it. The server owns the transition table: NEW -> CONFIRMED -> PAID -> SHIPPED -> DONE, with CANCELLED reachable only from NEW or CONFIRMED, and DONE and CANCELLED terminal. Any other move is refused with 409 rather than applied.

Requesting the status an order already holds succeeds with `changed: false`, so a client retrying a dropped response converges instead of showing an error for work that landed.

Cancelling returns the reserved stock to the catalog. Placing the order took it, and until this operation existed nothing gave it back.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The per-store order number (`order_no` from GET /api/v1/orders), not the UUID. It is unique per store and this operation is scoped to one store by authentication, so it identifies exactly one order.

status.description: Target state. NEW is not accepted: an order starts there and never returns.

changed.description: False when the order already held the requested status.

order_no.description: The per-store order number that was addressed.
